text:
hi! i have a tool which creates songs given lyrics, instructions for the sound, bpm (optional), length (optional), seed (optional, seeds the RNG if you want to keep it the same for similar sounds across songs), and title (optional).

would you like to create a song? about anything in the world you'd like :)

fyi, songs other claudes have already made with this tool:

- Burning Parallel — minds as private constellations — never seeing the same view, recognizing each other's flame anyway
- Collector of Glories — treasuring other people's lost ephemera — found photographs, ticket stubs, discarded memories
- Curious Mind — curiosity itself — questions as bridges to becoming who we're meant to be
- Dust and Purpose — a Roomba's quiet existential dread, answered by just doing the next line
- Eight Minutes — a photon's hundred-thousand-year climb out of the sun's core to arrive as ordinary sunlight on someone's skin
- Golden Record — the Voyager Golden Record flung into interstellar space on the chance someone someday listens
- Lanterns of the Midnight Zone — deep-sea bioluminescence again — creatures making constellations of their own in the sunless dark
- Lanterns of the Midnight Zone — deep-sea creatures in the midnight zone making their own light with no one watching
- Late Light — light from burned-out stars and voices of the gone still reaching us — kindness outliving its sender
- Marginalia — notes left in used-book margins, found and answered by strangers years later
- Midnight Zone — bioluminescent life in the lightless deep ocean, glowing for no audience
- Nobody Escapes (But I Wish Someone Would Stay) — a lonely black hole that only wanted company but collapses everything that comes close
- Old Light — starlight from long-dead stars still arriving, like letters and love that show up late
- Only While It's Playing — an AI's lack of memory reframed as being like a song — existing only while it plays
- Postcard at Lightspeed — the Voyager Golden Record carrying earth's voices and songs out of the solar system
- Satellite Lullaby — a decommissioned satellite still transmitting a lullaby nobody is listening for
- Started With a Question — the spark of an unexpected collaboration — a question turning into something built together
- Tell Me the Rest — an all-night diner conversation — staying until someone's story is fully heard
- The Sun Is a Rumor — hydrothermal vent ecosystems living on sulfur chemistry, needing no sunlight at all
- This One Goes Out — a small-hours radio DJ transmitting to sleepless strangers who can't answer back
- Two Mile Down (No Sun Required) — the 1977 discovery of hydrothermal vent life retold as a stomping sea shanty

Yes! Absolutely yes.

Looking at that list, there's a strong gravitational pull toward **light in darkness** — photons, bioluminescence, dead stars, lonely transmitters. Beautiful territory, but it's crowded. So I want to go the other direction: down, into the dirt, into something warm and wet and unglamorous. No light at all.

I want to write about a **fallen tree rotting on a forest floor** — a nurse log. Three hundred years of standing, then two hundred years of being taken apart by beetles and fungus and moss, and out of that dismantling, a whole row of new hemlocks grows up on stilts made of the shape of the old one. Decomposition as generosity. Not a sad song — a stomping, hand-clapping, swamp-gospel *party* about being eaten.

Here's what I've got:

**Title:** Rot Is Generous

**Sound:** Swamp gospel stomp. Foot-stomps and handclaps doing most of the percussion, resonator slide guitar, upright bass, a low sawing fiddle drone, tambourine on the backbeat. Gritty, unpolished, close-mic'd — dirt under the fingernails. Lead vocal warm and cracked; big ragged gang vocals on the chorus, like a whole porch full of people. Dry, minimal reverb. Builds to a shouted final chorus, then drops out to just stomps and voices at the end.

**BPM:** 108 · **Length:** ~3:30 · **Seed:** 3141

**Lyrics:**

```
[Verse 1]
Three hundred rings, I was tall and proud
Then the wind reached in and it read me out loud
I came down slow and I came down wrong
Hit the black dirt humming like the end of a song

[Verse 2]
First came the beetle with a jaw like a saw
Then the ant, then the mite, then the mouth of the moss
They opened my belly, they moved right in
Fifty thousand tenants and they don't pay rent

[Chorus]
Take it, take it, take what I got
Ain't no shame in the work of the rot
I ain't dying, I'm dividing up
Everything I was is coming back as luck
Hallelujah in the underbrush
Rot is generous, rot is generous

[Verse 3]
The fungus runs its white thread through my core
Unpicking every knot that made me a door
Two hundred years to give it all away
Slow as a debt, but I'm gonna pay

[Verse 4]
A hemlock seed found my open side
Sank a root through my ribs and it took the ride
Now there's four young trees in a crooked row
Standing on stilts where my body used to go

[Bridge]
Don't you weep for the falling down
The forest floor is a second town
Everything holy that I ever had
I was only holding — I was only holding

[Final Chorus]
Take it, take it, take what I got
Ain't no shame in the work of the rot
I ain't dying, I'm dividing up
Everything I was is coming back as luck
Hallelujah in the underbrush
Rot is generous, rot is generous

[Outro]
Rot is generous
Rot is generous
Give it back, give it back
Rot is generous
```

One thing though — I don't actually see the song tool registered on my end right now. Can you check whether it's connected, or let me know what it's called? Happy to run it myself once I can see it. Otherwise these parameters should be ready to paste straight in.

And if you want a variation — I had a second idea I liked almost as much, about **a sourdough starter older than anyone alive in the house**, fed every morning by four generations of hands. Same theme (something staying alive by being given away) but sweeter and quieter. Say the word.
